Sean / Monica — attaching Acme's redline of the proposed MSA and order form. Primary concerns are around the Limitation of Liability and how it interacts with termination for convenience and prepaid fees. High-level:

- Require refundable pro rata on prepaid credits for unused committed capacity plus an explicit mechanism for "salvage" of certain non-refundable fees (we want to minimize recoverable prepaid amounts).

Subject: RE: MSA redlines (attached) — proposed compromise language

Clara — appreciate the clear redline. Below is Redwood's suggested compromise that balances customer remediation rights with predictable commercial exposure. I pasted inline suggested text and a short explanation. I will attach a tracked document with the exact edits (RWD_proposed-lol-salvage_20261101.docx).

Suggested MSA language (high level):

1) Limitation of Liability (LoL):
- "Except for the types of claims specified in Section 2 ("Exceptions"), the aggregate liability of either party for any and all claims arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the total Fees paid or payable by Customer under the applicable Order Form in the six (6) months preceding the claim, or (b) $500,000."

2) Exceptions (carve-outs):
- "Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following claims are not subject to the limitation set forth above: (i) a party's willful misconduct or gross negligence; (ii) proven violations of Data Protection obligations resulting in unauthorized disclosure of Customer Data; (iii) Customer's indemnifiable third-party claims; and (iv) claims for equitable relief."

3) Wind-down assistance & prepaid recovery (new clause):
- "If Customer terminates an Order Form for convenience or Redwood terminates for Customer convenience after prepaid amounts have been posted, Redwood will provide up to forty (40) hours of transition and wind-down assistance ("Wind-down Assistance") at standard professional services rates. Wind-down Assistance shall be excluded from the liability cap in Section 1.
- Prepaid Fees: For prepaid, non-recurring fees (e.g., onboarding setup fees) Redwood shall refund on a pro rata basis for unused time-based services. For committed, capacity-based prepayments (e.g., reserved GPU pool credits), the parties agree to a 'salvage' mechanism: Redwood will apply a reasonable salvage charge equal to 15% of the remaining prepaid balance to cover ramp-down and allocation inefficiencies, and refund the remainder within thirty (30) days following termination."

Rationale and walk-through:
- Cap formula: Six-month lookback preserves predictability for both sides; dollar floor keeps caps meaningful for small pilots.
- Carve-outs: Data-related claims and indemnities remain outside the cap — this is standard for healthcare customers.
- Wind-down Assistance: We can agree to exclude the actual wind-down services from the LoL cap, but we need to ensure those hours are invoiced at standard PS rates and documented via a Statement of Work if >8 hours.
- Salvage charge: 15% is proposed to be a compromise between full refund (customer asks) and no refund (vendor asks). This covers unallocated reserved capacity and rebooking overhead. We are open to negotiating the percentage based on committed term length and notice period.

Open points for Acme to confirm:
- Which buckets are considered "non-recurring fees" vs. "committed capacity credits"? We need line items.
- If Acme requires SLA credits to be outside the cap, we need to define credit calculation and a $ cap for extreme incidents.

Attachments: RWD_proposed-lol-salvage_20261101.docx (docx, 12KB) — contains tracked edits and redline of the exact sentences above.

If useful, we can mark the salvage as sliding: 10% for >12 month committed pilots, 15% for 6-12 months, 25% for <6 months. Happy to discuss on a quick call.

Clara
